item.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
item.description: For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Sumer Loggins

item.title: COP31 negotiations break down as countries fail to agree on climate deal
item.description: A fight over whether to mention fossil fuels caused the talks, which had become the longest in summit history, to fall apart. It was the first such collapse in over a decade. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Taz Ali, Victoria Bisset, Sarah Kaplan, Jake Spring, Mary Ilyushina

item.title: A firefly not seen since 1983 has been found again after scientist recognised its amber flashes
item.description: Exciting news emerged in 2026 when a firefly, thought to have vanished since 1983, was rediscovered in Delaware and Virginia. Its unique amber flash patterns caught the attention of researchers, confirming its survival. Habitat loss is suspected to have led to its absence from earlier records. Community engagement significantly aided in this rediscovery, prompting further surveys to assess the firefly's population and habitat requirements. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
item.description: European and vulnerable nations rejected a proposed agreement after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas. Publicado también por: Africanews. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan and Lisa Friedman

item.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen emerges as a major nutrient source for global oceans
item.description: A research team has quantified an important component of the global nitrogen cycle. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find 156-million-year-old horned reptile fossil in Wyoming sandstone
item.description: A remarkable discovery in Wyoming has unearthed a fossil of a diminutive dinosaur-like creature, dating back 156 million years to the Jurassic era. Advanced imaging techniques uncovered this skeleton entombed in sandstone. Researchers classify it as an early reptilian branch, enhancing our understanding of evolutionary history. Analysis indicates it inhabited freshwater environments and may have fallen prey to a larger predator. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: JWST finds a possible black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy in the early universe
item.description: How the first massive black holes formed in the universe remains an open question in astronomy. Black holes weighing about a billion solar masses within the first billion years of the universe require extraordinary origin stories. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
item.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected
item.description: EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global… Publicado también por: ABC News Australia. Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Fiona Harvey and Graham Readfearn in Antalya

item.title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
item.description: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet's mountain of mysteries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
item.description: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat Sunday after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hybrid nanocrystal surface reveals new way to tune interactions with infrared light
item.description: A one-crystal-thick sheet made from two types of nanocrystals mixed in solution can amplify or suppress infrared light beyond the sum of its parts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La Cumbre del Clima de la ONU fracasó en llegar a un acuerdo por el uso de los combustibles fósiles
item.description: La Unión Europea, Panamá, las Islas Marshall y otros países rechazaron el borrador del acuerdo final de la COP31 porque no incluye ninguna referencia a los combustibles fósiles ni a la transición para abandonar su uso. Tras más de 44 horas de prórroga, las negociaciones continúan estancadas y la cumbre corre el riesgo de concluir sin un acuerdo definitivo. Nuestro corresponsal, Adrià Rocha, nos amplía la información. Publicado también por: France 24 - Español, Clarín - Mundo. Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Australia urged to wean off imported fossil fuels amid global supply shocks
item.description: Grattan Institute report calls on government to ‘seize’ opportunity to cap diesel tax credits, introduce EV subsidies for less wealthy’ and build ‘clean’ refineries Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Capping lucrative diesel tax handouts to big business, building new “clean” refineries and targeting electric vehicle subsidies to less wealthy people could save Australians thousands of dollars in fuel per year, according to a major new report calling on the government to reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels. The Grattan Institute, one of the nation’s most… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Josh Butler

item.title: La NASA está reclutando astronautas para vivir en la luna a -203 °C con polvo abrasivo y sueldos de 164.000 dólares
item.description: Desde el pasado 7 de noviembre, si quieres irte a vivir a la luna, puedes presentar tu candidatura a la NASA. Ahora, ya te adelanto que no es tan fácil como presentar los papeles para una VPO. La Administración Nacional de Aeronáutica y el Espacio estadounidense ha abierto su convocatoria para su próxima hornada de astronautas. Un pequeño detallito sin importancia: la base lunar de la NASA todavía no existe. Pero no hay mal que por bien no venga: más tiempo para prepararse. ¿Quién quiere vivir en la luna? Esta nueva generación de astronautas recibirá un entrenamiento para operar en la… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Eva R. de Luis

item.title: Milky Way simulation reaches record resolution with the help of three supercomputers
item.description: A team of researchers, including those from the University of Tokyo, have developed a new way to model the Milky Way at a level of detail never achieved before. They simulated the entire galaxy down to the level of individual stars by combining the power of some of the world's most powerful supercomputers using an AI-accelerated model that works on a variety of hardware platforms. Their methods can improve our understanding of galactic evolution. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Parasite makes mice more attractive to blood-feeding bugs, which may aid its spread
item.description: Some parasites, such as Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi, can be passed between mammals and blood-feeding insects called triatomine bugs. Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
item.description: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
item.description: Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: BepiColombo, la misión a Mercurio que busca descubrir por qué el planeta se está achicando (y otros misterios)
item.description: Una nave espacial llamada BepiColombo está llegando este mes a nuestro vecino menos explorado, con la esperanza de arrojar luz sobre algunos de sus misterios. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Carnegie Museum will prepare three sauropods in public; researchers study rare skin samples
item.description: Three sauropod fossils from Wyoming, nicknamed Daisy, Lucky, and Lucy, are headed for Pittsburgh. A $5 million donation from Ken Griffin will construct a public fossil preparation laboratory at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History. Visitors will be able to observe the cleaning and studying process of these 150-million-year-old dinosaurs. Additionally, research will focus on rare fossilized skin samples associated with the fossils. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.description: Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: New COP31 draft deal tabled as countries scramble to salvage climate talks
item.description: The latest draft again failed to mention fossil fuels, which have become a flashpoint at the talks. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: Algo raro está pasando alrededor de la Tierra: temporalmente nuestros dos cinturones de radiación se hicieron cuatro y nadie sabe por qué
item.description: Si la Tierra no tuviese un campo magnético a su alrededor , sufriría el bombardeo constante de partículas ionizadas muy energéticas procedentes del Sol y de los rayos cósmicos. Por suerte, contamos con este escudo que desvía la mayor parte de esas partículas y, a su vez, retiene algunas en dos anillos, conocidos como cinturones de Van Allen . Si están ahí retenidas, no pueden hacernos daños, pero más vale que nuestros satélites o naves espaciales no crucen estos anillos, pues sería muy peligroso para los que no estén preparados. Esta es la razón por la que es importante estudiarlos como ha… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: COP31: Turkiye's final draft doesn't mention the words ‘fossil fuels’ that cause global warming
item.description: COP31 President Murat Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: COP31 struggles to reach deal with parties at odds over fossil fuels
item.description: The language around fossil fuels remains a flashpoint at UN climate talks in Türkiye, where negotiations have gone into a second day past the deadline. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Single feathers may reveal whether eastern black rails stay in Texas or migrate north
item.description: High-stepping like you're in a marching band while dragging a rope through a wetland at night can make you wonder about your life choices. Several plastic bottles, each filled with two or three noisy cat toys, are attached to the rope. It's pitch black, and all I can hear are the cat toys jingling, the mosquitoes buzzing in my ears and the wetland grasses bouncing in the wind. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Informe desde Estambul: negociaciones en la COP31 estancadas por los combustibles fósiles
item.description: La COP31, celebrada en Antalya (Turquía), entró en una fase de estancamiento debido a uno de los temas más polémicos de la agenda climática: el futuro de los combustibles fósiles. Mientras un bloque de países exige que el acuerdo final incluya un compromiso explícito sobre los combustibles fósiles. Naciones productoras como Arabia Saudita y Rusia se oponen. Desde Estambul, nuestro corresponsal Adria Rocha nos da los detalles. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: With the rise of online shopping, rural main streets are changing
item.description: As Longreach locals watch the town's main street pivot towards a growing government and legal sector, some researchers say there is opportunity in buildings left empty by the digital sales transition. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Jay Carstens

item.title: The avian champions of long-distance migration keep surprising scientists
item.description: "The whole story began with an extinct bird from Hispaniola," said Min Zhao, a former postdoctoral associate at the Florida Museum of Natural History (now a postdoctoral researcher at Uppsala University). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers tracked a long-legged bird’s migration. He flew 6,800 miles.
item.description: Conservationists say the journey made by the bird, a bar-tailed godwit called Phil, was an "incredible feat." Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Dhruti Shah

item.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
item.description: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
item.description: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down
item.description: Most materials get weaker with use. But a team led by Chenfeng Ke, a professor of chemistry in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, has created a polymer that defies the usual laws of wear and tear. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists flew drones through humpback whales' breath off Canada and sequenced entire genomes
item.description: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have pioneered a groundbreaking technique to harness whale DNA through the use of drones. This method captures genetic material from the whales' breath, often referred to as whale snot. Their findings successfully sequenced complete genomes from specimens gathered off the coast of British Columbia. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Dropping degree requirements linked to higher pay for workers without degrees
item.description: The requirements set by human resources (HR) greatly influence the professional opportunities available to different segments of the population. For instance, if a job requires applicants to have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant subject, people without them may be excluded from the selection process, even if they have gained relevant skills through experience or professional training. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million to anyone who can solve one big problem standing in the way of building a human settlement on the Moon
item.description: NASA has launched the Moon Base Challenge, encouraging students to develop solutions for lunar habitation. The initiative offers $1 million in prizes to student teams from high schools and universities. Teams will focus on areas like power generation, life-support systems, and astronaut safety to address the complexities of lunar living. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, 2027, to eligible educational institutions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a… Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
item.description: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest
item.description: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: En 1988 una nave soviética se perdió en el espacio. Ahora, un astrónomo cree haberla encontrado en un misterioso asteroide
item.description: Recientemente hablamos en Xataka sobre 1998 KY26, un asteroide misterioso que muestra una aceleración anómala para este tipo de objetos espaciales. Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que se trataba de algo conocido como cometa oscuro, pero un estudio reciente demostró que el asteroide está demasiado caliente para encajar en esa hipótesis. A partir de ahí, todas las esperanzas se depositaron en Hayabusa 2, la nave japonesa que, después de completar su misión en el asteroide Ryugu, había puesto rumbo a resolver este enigma. Desgraciadamente, la agencia espacial de Japón, JAXA, acaba de anunciar la… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
item.description: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
item.description: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously. Using atomic clocks with dramatically enhanced sensitivity, researchers hope to reveal a never-before-observed quantum effect that could transform our understanding of time and gravity. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath
item.description: Astronomers have witnessed a spectacular cosmic collision in the Andromeda galaxy, where a small star spiraled into a giant star 18,000 times brighter than the Sun, triggering a violent eruption. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured the aftermath just 47 days later, revealing new details about how two stars can merge into one. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved
item.description: A mysterious skeleton discovered in a Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey may finally be identified after more than 150 years. New dating evidence suggests the remains belonged to a high-ranking medieval abbot who was buried inside a centuries-old recycled Roman coffin. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
item.description: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is
item.description: Scientists cannot agree on what science actually is, and a new study finds their views are surprisingly more divided than those of the general public. The findings could help explain public frustration with scientific uncertainty and raise questions about how artificial intelligence might reshape future discoveries. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists say the human family tree may need a radical rewrite
item.description: The human family tree may need a major overhaul. New research from Monash University challenges the traditional classification of our ancient ancestors, arguing that species such as Australopithecus and Paranthropus should be grouped within our own genus, Homo. As scientists uncover more fossils and analyze evolutionary relationships, the boundaries that once separated these ancient relatives are becoming increasingly difficult to defend. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Fermi's 14-year all-sky map bridges astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'
item.description: Gamma rays, the most high-energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. We've always had trouble measuring them in the "megaelectronvolt" (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the "MeV gap." But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
item.description: Modern genetics does not support claims of innate racial differences in intelligence. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan R. Goodman and Rebecca Sear, The Conversation

item.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies
item.description: Three years ago, a schoolteacher in Norway was reprimanded for putting his pupils' iPads aside to return to pen and paper. Now, the whole country is rethinking its approach to new technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fossil fuel row sees COP31 talks spill into overtime
item.description: A number of countries, including France and Panama, released a letter on Friday insisting that a deal include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels." Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: La COP31 se prolonga sin acuerdo por las diferencias sobre combustibles fósiles y financiación climática
item.description: La COP31 continuó este sábado en Antalya, Turquía, más allá de su cierre previsto, ante la falta de consenso sobre la salida de los combustibles fósiles y la financiación para los países en desarrollo. La Unión Europea y Panamá advirtieron que no respaldarán un texto que no responda a sus exigencias, mientras los negociadores intentan acercar posiciones. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: AFP

item.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
item.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
item.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Device that measures strawberry skin's strength will aid breeders
item.description: Resilient strawberry varieties will be more easily identifiable thanks to a tool developed by University of Queensland engineering students. The prototype measures the strength of strawberry skin, a key breeding consideration for the Australian Strawberry Breeding Program at Queensland's Department of Primary Industries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum software matches classical benchmark for a molecular interaction
item.description: Predicting how molecules interact is central to drug discovery: it offers important information about how a new drug might work in the human body, the side effects it can cause and more. Computationally modeling these interactions can reduce the need for lengthy and expensive lab work, but some interactions still remain beyond the reach of classical computers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
item.description: Microplastics may be doing something far more dangerous than simply accumulating in our bodies. Scientists have discovered that tiny plastic particles can interact with water to generate highly reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. This unexpected chemical activity could help explain growing evidence linking microplastic exposure to serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and neurological disorders. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it
item.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 has reached an extraordinary milestone, traveling 16.1 billion miles from Earth to become the first spacecraft so distant that its signals take a full day to reach us. Nearly 50 years after launch, the aging probe continues its historic journey through interstellar space, pushing the limits of human exploration despite dwindling power and technical challenges. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
item.description: After eight years and 10 billion kilometers in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope heading to Mercury has captured its first cosmic observations and is performing even better than scientists expected. The instrument could soon reveal Mercury's hidden chemical secrets and transform our understanding of how the solar system's smallest planet formed. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The call of the seamount: Two new armored tardigrades described in the Atlantic
item.description: An international team led by researchers from Senckenberg am Meer in Wilhelmshaven has described two new species of marine tardigrades. The tiny marine organisms were discovered in the sediment of the Senghor Seamount off the coast of Cape Verde. According to the researchers, the discovery underscores the role of undersea mountains as oases of biodiversity. The study, which includes comprehensive taxonomic descriptions of the new species, has been published in the journal "ZooKeys." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet
item.description: A promising material for ultra-fast optical communications has held a secret for decades, but scientists may have finally cracked it. Researchers at KAIST and Caltech have precisely measured how barium titanate controls and absorbs light, resolving longstanding uncertainties that have slowed its development. Their findings could make it easier to build optical devices that transmit information faster while wasting less light. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: BepiColombo finally reaches Mercury after eight-year odyssey
item.description: Nature, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03803-8 European and Japanese probes will trace different paths around the planet to study its surface and its surroundings. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Davide Castelvecchi

item.title: Hatching a plan to ensure Australia's native turtles survive and thrive
item.description: How a citizen science program is saving thousands of turtles even as researchers learn more about them. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Gavin McGrath

item.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
item.description: EU warns COP31 risks turning into a 'fossil summit' as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
item.description: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds
item.description: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
item.description: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist
item.description: The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions
item.description: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
item.description: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users
item.description: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms
item.description: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New NASA Seed Funding Primes Small Businesses for Innovation
item.description: Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Abby Tabor

item.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
item.description: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New hemp plant produces no detectable THC, potentially reducing risk of crop destruction
item.description: Scientists at Texas A&M AgriLife Research, a member of The Texas A&M University System, have developed a hemp plant that produces no detectable cannabinoids, including THC. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
item.description: "We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated." Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations
item.description: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model can detect stress in agricultural crops using a nondestructive imaging technique, allowing changes in crop health to be monitored over time. Developed by a team of researchers at Penn State, the new model shows promise for accurately detecting crop stress caused by drought, disease, nutrient deficiency and other causes while using less computing power than some existing AI methods. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can Instagram reduce prejudice? Study reveals the potential and limits of social media contact
item.description: A research team at the University of Potsdam has conducted a field experiment to investigate whether contact through social media can reduce prejudice. The findings suggest that following an unfamiliar Instagram profile for just three days can lead to more favorable attitudes—not only toward the group represented by the profile. The study was published in the Journal of the Association for Information Systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How a season without their 'admiral' showed the Rockets what they were missing
item.description: Fred VanVleet is commanding the surging Rockets after an ACL injury derailed his 2025-26 season. Fuente: ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Wright

item.title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss
item.description: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. If glaciers border a lake, the water can melt the ice from underneath; furthermore, chunks of ice can break off and fall into the lake. The extent to which these processes influence the situation, compared with other factors, had not been sufficiently clarified at a global level until now. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: X-ray technique advances temperature measurements under extreme pressure
item.description: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have advanced the ability to measure temperatures in materials subjected to extreme pressures at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), providing new insights into how materials behave under conditions relevant to national security and high-energy-density physics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Parasite protein expands understanding of how mitochondria build their ribosomes
item.description: Mitochondria are essential components of the cells of most organisms, including humans. They are often referred to as the cell's powerhouses because they produce the energy needed for cellular functions. However, mitochondria originally evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells in the distant past. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Amazon communities have a complicated relationship with giant anacondas; a 2025 study explores why some people fear them while others live alongside them
item.description: Communities in the Lower Amazon have a multifaceted relationship with giant anacondas, dealing with folklore and livestock concerns. The presence of these snakes is often rooted in local myths, but practical encounters create conflicts. Killing anacondas frequently stems from protecting domestic animals rather than pure fear. Researchers indicate that the people's perceptions of the snakes have altered due to economic considerations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale
item.description: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El Niño created a skiers' paradise in Chile—now it's Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies' turn
item.description: El Niño has a reputation for being a skier's dream, bringing lots of snow to California's Sierra Nevada and the southern Rockies. Tahoe-area resorts were already seeing the effects in mid-November 2026 as several feet of snow fell and some resorts prepared to open early for the season. But El Niño's supercharged precipitation can spell trouble, too. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Practical organ-on-a-chip platform helps assess the toxicity of environmental chemicals
item.description: Among the thousands of chemicals used in daily life, toxicity information is available for only a small fraction. Much of this information comes from high-dose animal studies, which are costly, time-consuming and limited by species differences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New sources of neurotoxin linked to algal blooms uncovered in Florida and Kansas
item.description: Researchers have identified two previously unreported strains of freshwater cyanobacteria capable of producing a potent neurotoxin that poses risks to people, pets, wildlife and water resources and that some scientists suspect may have contributed to previous animal deaths. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bumblebees challenge long-held beliefs about brain size and intelligence
item.description: Bigger brains mean greater intelligence, or so conventional wisdom goes. After all, humans have much larger brains than most other animals and are generally considered the planet's most intelligent species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Is it genuine love—or obsessive passion? Kierkegaard, the father of existentialism, had some thoughts
item.description: Young love, honeymoon love, infatuation—these often feel spectacular. You have a burning need to be in constant contact, and you don't want to let that person out of your sight. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Witnessing generosity from low-income donors more likely to elicit giving from observers, research finds
item.description: Billionaire Warren Buffett announced this month he will donate $5.47 billion to four foundations associated with his family ahead of Thanksgiving. Similarly, various students in club organizations throughout Kansas are collecting food items to give to hungry families for the holiday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Spiders, beetles and one garage alligator: Largest study to date reveals wildlife sharing our indoor spaces
item.description: An international team of researchers is revealing the largest study to date detailing the wide range of insects, arachnids and other organisms that live in homes and other indoor environments across the United States and Canada. The researchers have compiled a database with more than 20,000 entries spanning more than 2,000 species found in these indoor ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Deep Venture: A new class of ocean exploration vehicle developed
item.description: Researchers have a new capability for exploring some of the least understood regions of the ocean. Developed by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) in collaboration with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Deep Venture is a next-generation autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) for deep-ocean research, capable of supporting a wide range of scientific missions, from shallow coastal waters to the deepest places on Earth. It can withstand extreme pressure, rated for depths of up to 11,000 meters (about 6.83 mi), or full ocean depth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Anthropic researcher says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, first posed in 1859
item.description: A researcher at AI company Anthropic said Friday that he had used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A new way to extract oxygen from lunar soil could support bases on the moon
item.description: Computer chip manufacturing and lunar exploration seem like completely different worlds. Yet our latest research suggests the two may be more closely connected than expected. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Theory explains how fusion plasmas enter a state of improved energy confinement, solving a 40-year puzzle
item.description: Nuclear fusion promises a source of energy by combining light atomic nuclei, the same process that powers the sun. To achieve fusion on Earth, scientists must heat a gas to extreme temperatures, creating a charged state of matter called plasma. Keeping this plasma hot and stable long enough for fusion energy production is one of the main challenges facing the technology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: U.K.'s nature health check doesn't stack up in wildlife's favor—but volunteers are collecting plenty of crucial data
item.description: As nature declines over time, it becomes easier to normalize an increasingly impoverished environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP31 logra acuerdos de inversión, pero persisten las diferencias sobre los combustibles fósiles
item.description: Aunque estaba previsto que las negociaciones de la COP31 concluyeran este 20 de noviembre, aún no se han alcanzado acuerdos definitivos sobre los combustibles fósiles. Turquía anunció acuerdos y proyectos de inversión por más de 26.000 millones de dólares. Por su parte, la financiación climática para los países en desarrollo continúa siendo uno de los principales puntos de desacuerdo. Nuestro corresponsal, Adrià Rocha, nos amplía los detalles. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Killer whales became fearsome predators long before scientists thought
item.description: Killer whales, or orcas, are among the ocean's most formidable predators, hunting everything from fish and seals to other whales. But how and when these members of the dolphin family evolved into such effective hunters has long been something of a mystery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How desert biocrusts respond to changing snow cover
item.description: In the desert, winter snow may seem like a temporary visitor, but its effects can last long after the snow melts. By supplying water to dry ecosystems, snowfall helps sustain biological soil crusts (biocrusts), thin living layers on the soil surface that play important roles in desert ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Excitons mimic light in atom-thin material, confirming decade-old quantum prediction
item.description: Combining their skills in theory and experiment, Yale researchers have observed for the first time a type of energy-carrying composite particle move in a highly unexpected way. It's a finding that could lead to advances in quantum technologies, solar energy, LEDs and other optoelectronic technologies. The work is published in Nature Physics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Honor Awards Ceremony Recognizes Employees at Stennis Space Center
item.description: Employees contributing to NASA’s mission at the agency’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, were recognized during the center’s Honor Awards ceremony on Nov. 18. Presenting the awards were Christine Powell, NASA Stennis center director, and Jeremy Parsons, the agency’s Artemis program manager responsible for management and oversight of NASA’s initiative to return […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: LaToya Dean

item.title: Researchers trace shifting pulsation modes in δ Scuti star KIC 4737720
item.description: Stars in the night sky may look calm and unchanging, but some are in fact constantly "vibrating." Just as a musical instrument can sound several notes at once, a star can pulse in several modes simultaneously. By measuring minute changes in a star's brightness, astronomers can read these stellar vibrations and, in turn, probe the physical processes at work inside it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Venus-like conditions reveal how minerals could preserve traces of ancient water
item.description: Venus is one of the most inhospitable environments in our solar system, with surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead and atmospheric pressure nearly 100 times greater than Earth's. Yet its surface may preserve clues to a time when the planet looked much more like Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Male bumblebees contribute to nest care, challenging view that they only mate
item.description: For decades, researchers have assumed male bumblebees' contribution to hives consisted mainly of DNA. However, a new study finds that the males actually help incubate baby bumbles, and that with males' assistance, hives thrive. The study, published in the Royal Society Open Science journal, quantifies the beneficial effects of having male babysitters in the hive. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover Collects Samples
item.description: This Nov. 16 collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. Learn more […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Misinformation perception shapes support of democracy in Australia
item.description: A new study by Adelaide University researchers has found that the more often people perceived they had encountered misinformation, the less positive their views of Australian democracy tended to be. The experience-sampling study from the School of Psychology asked 123 eligible voters to track their perceived exposure to misinformation in the lead-up to the 2025 Australian federal election and measured whether this exposure influenced their attitudes and emotions toward the election. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Low-viscosity lavas reveal a key to Mars's past
item.description: Since 2021, the Mars Perseverance rover has been roaming Jezero Crater, gathering details about the red planet's geology and hints about its past. On its journey, the rover took close-up images of the Séítah formation, a nearly 4-billion-year-old layer of rock at the base of the crater. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP31 climate talks go into overtime as nations quarrel over fossil fuels
item.description: The COP31 climate conference slipped into overtime on Friday as negotiators from nearly 200 ⁠countries struggled to bridge deep divisions ⁠over fossil fuels and climate finance. Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference ⁠heaped pressure on host Turkey and lead negotiator Australia, saying the meeting was on track to be the “worst COP ever” because it lacked ambition to address the worsening climate crisis. The biggest points of tension centre around whether a final deal should... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone
item.description: Russia launched a Soyuz rocket with satellites to help enable drone attacks over Ukraine. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: Activists protest failure of COP31 to advance on moving away from fossil fuels
item.description: Civil society groups and activists on Friday protested against UN climate talks' failure to advance ideas to move away from fossils fuels. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com (Rédaction Africanews)

item.title: NASA's powerful Moon rocket engine roars through a dramatic 200-second test
item.description: NASA has successfully tested a powerful RS-25 rocket engine, firing it for 200 seconds to gather data that could make future Moon missions safer and more reliable. The test supports preparations for the 2028 Artemis IV Moon landing and NASA’s ultimate ambition of sending astronauts to Mars. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
item.description: A new clinical trial found that the ketogenic diet dramatically outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat diets in reducing liver fat and improving metabolic health, even when participants lost similar amounts of weight. After just four to five months, about half of those following keto no longer met the criteria for prediabetes, while their liver fat dropped by an average of 67%. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists turn Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks for future lunar bases
item.description: Scientists have found a way to 3D-print Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks, raising the possibility of building lunar bases using materials already on the Moon. The experimental blocks still need to be strengthened, but the technology could transform how humans construct permanent settlements beyond Earth. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
item.description: Scientists at CERN have found the first evidence of an incredibly rare particle decay after more than 40 years of searching, detecting a process expected to occur just once in every 10 billion beauty particles. The breakthrough could help physicists explore a mysterious microscopic realm where unknown particles and forces may be hiding. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's
item.description: Reading for pleasure may have surprisingly powerful benefits for the brain, with studies linking it to better memory, reduced stress, improved mental health, and a lower risk of dementia. Researchers highlight findings that just five minutes of fiction can reduce stress by up to 20%, while reading has also been associated with a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: France awaits verdict in landmark police brutality trial over Michel Zecler assault
item.description: A French prosecutor on Thursday urged a court to jail three policemen who beat up a black music producer to four to six years, in a rare case of alleged police brutality to go to criminal court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic but authorities and law enforcement unions claim is limited to isolated cases. The prosecutor argued the case had caused "immense harm to Michel Zecler but also to society as a whole," and that those on trial had "betrayed" their uniform. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Somos casi tan pobres hoy como en 2018
item.description: La economía española ni va como una moto ni como un cohete y ni siquiera es la que más crece entre los países de la Unión Europea. Leer Fuente: Expansión - Economía.
item.dc:creator: Clemente Polo
